passages.text: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
passages.sermon:
John is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nHe writes to believers.
\r\nHe calls them his little children.
\r\nHe writes these things to them.
\r\nHe wants them not to sin.
\r\nIf anyone does sin, there is hope.
\r\nWe have an advocate with the Father.
\r\nThis advocate is Jesus Christ.
\r\nJesus Christ is righteous.
passages.original: Τεκνία μου ταῦτα γράφω ὑμῖν ἵνα μὴ ἁμάρτητε καὶ ἐάν τις ἁμάρτῃ Παράκλητον ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν δίκαιον

passages.text: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is righteous.
Jesus Christ is the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
He gave Himself for our sins.
He is not the sacrifice for our sins only.
He is also the sacrifice for the sins of the whole world.
passages.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἱλασμός ἐστιν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν οὐ περὶ τῶν ἡμετέρων δὲ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ ὅλου τοῦ κόσμου

passages.text: By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
passages.sermon: We can know that we have come to know Jesus.\r\nWe know this if we keep His commandments.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐγνώκαμεν αὐτόν ἐὰν τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν

passages.text: If anyone says, “I know Him,” but does not keep His commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
passages.sermon:
A person may say, "I know Him."
This person claims to know Jesus Christ.
If this person does not keep Jesus' commandments, he is a liar.
The truth is not in this person.
passages.original: ὁ λέγων ὅτι Ἔγνωκα αὐτόν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ μὴ τηρῶν ψεύστης ἐστίν καὶ ἐν τούτῳ ἡ ἀλήθεια οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: But if anyone keeps His word, the love of God has been truly perfected in him. By this we know that we are in Him: Whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked.
passages.sermon:
Anyone who keeps God's word shows something important.
God's love has been made complete in that person.
This is how we know we are in God.
Anyone who says, "I remain in God," must live as Jesus lived.
Jesus obeyed God and loved others.
We must also obey God and love others, just as Jesus did.
passages.original: ὃς δ’ ἂν τηρῇ αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον ἀληθῶς ἐν τούτῳ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Θεοῦ τετελείωται Ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐσμεν ὁ λέγων ἐν αὐτῷ μένειν ὀφείλει καθὼς ἐκεῖνος περιεπάτησεν καὶ αὐτὸς οὕτως περιπατεῖν

passages.text: Beloved, I am not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one, which you have had from the beginning. This commandment is the message you have heard.
passages.sermon:
Beloved, I am writing to you.
I am not giving you a new commandment.
I am giving you an old commandment.
You have had this commandment from the beginning.
This old commandment is the message you have heard.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητοί οὐκ ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἐντολὴν παλαιὰν ἣν εἴχετε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ παλαιά ἐστιν ὁ λόγος ὃν ἠκούσατε

passages.text: Then again, I am also writing to you a new commandment, which is true in Him and also in you. For the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining.
passages.sermon:
John is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
John writes to believers in Jesus.
John gives a new commandment to the believers.
This new commandment is true in Jesus.
This new commandment is also true in the believers.
The darkness is passing away.
The true light is already shining.
passages.original: πάλιν ἐντολὴν καινὴν γράφω ὑμῖν ὅ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ σκοτία παράγεται καὶ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ἤδη φαίνει

passages.text: If anyone claims to be in the light but hates his brother, he is still in the darkness.
passages.sermon:
John writes to Christians.
He teaches about light and darkness.
He says, “If anyone claims to be in the light, but hates his brother, he is still in the darkness.”
A person may say, “I am in the light.”
If that person hates his brother, he is not in the light.
He remains in darkness.
passages.original: Ὁ λέγων ἐν τῷ φωτὶ εἶναι καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῶν ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἐστὶν ἕως ἄρτι

passages.text: Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
passages.sermon: Whoever loves his brother stays in the light.\r\nThere is nothing in him that causes others to stumble.
passages.original: ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ φωτὶ μένει καὶ σκάνδαλον ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness. He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
passages.sermon:
Whoever hates his brother lives in darkness.
He walks in darkness.
He does not know where he is going.
The darkness has blinded his eyes.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ ἐστὶν καὶ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ περιπατεῖ καὶ οὐκ οἶδεν ποῦ ὑπάγει ὅτι ἡ σκοτία ἐτύφλωσεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven through His name.
passages.sermon:
John is the writer.
John addresses believers as little children.
John writes to these little children.
God has forgiven their sins.
God forgave their sins because of Jesus’ name.
passages.original: Γράφω ὑμῖν τεκνία ὅτι ἀφέωνται ὑμῖν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι διὰ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.
passages.sermon:
Fathers, I am writing to you.
You know Him who is from the beginning.
Young men, I am writing to you.
You have overcome the evil one.
Children, I have written to you.
You know the Father.
passages.original: Γράφω ὑμῖν πατέρες ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς Γράφω ὑμῖν νεανίσκοι ὅτι νενικήκατε τὸν πονηρόν Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν παιδία ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν Πατέρα

passages.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
passages.sermon:
Fathers, I have written to you.
You know Him who is from the beginning.
Young men, I have written to you.
You are strong.
The word of God lives in you.
You have overcome the evil one.
passages.original: Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν πατέρες ὅτι ἐγνώκατε τὸν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν νεανίσκοι ὅτι ἰσχυροί ἐστε καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν μένει καὶ νενικήκατε τὸν πονηρόν

passages.text: Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
passages.sermon: Do not love the world.\r\nDo not love anything in the world.\r\nIf anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in that person.
passages.original: Μὴ ἀγαπᾶτε τὸν κόσμον μηδὲ τὰ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν κόσμον οὐκ ἔστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but from the world.
passages.sermon:
Everything in the world does not come from God the Father.
The world contains the desires of the flesh.
The world contains the desires of the eyes.
The world contains the pride of life.
These things do not come from the Father.
These things come from the world.
passages.original: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν καὶ ἡ ἀλαζονεία τοῦ βίου οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ πατρός ἀλλὰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἐστίν

passages.text: The world is passing away, along with its desires; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
passages.sermon: The world is passing away.\r\nIts desires are also passing away.\r\nWhoever does the will of God remains forever.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ κόσμος παράγεται καὶ ἡ ἐπιθυμία αὐτοῦ ὁ δὲ ποιῶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα

passages.text: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.
passages.sermon:
John speaks to believers as children.
He says, "It is the last hour."
Believers have heard that the antichrist is coming.
Now, many antichrists have already appeared.
This shows that it is the last hour.
passages.original: Παιδία ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν καὶ καθὼς ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἀντίχριστος ἔρχεται καὶ νῦν ἀντίχριστοι πολλοὶ γεγόνασιν ὅθεν γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν

passages.text: They went out from us, but they did not belong to us. For if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. But their departure made it clear that none of them belonged to us.
passages.sermon:
Some people left us.
They did not truly belong to us.
If they had belonged to us, they would have stayed with us.
Their leaving showed that not all of them were truly part of us.
passages.original: ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθαν ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν εἰ γὰρ ἐξ ἡμῶν ἦσαν μεμενήκεισαν ἂν μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἀλλ’ ἵνα φανερωθῶσιν ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν πάντες ἐξ ἡμῶν

passages.text: You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth.
passages.sermon:
You are believers in Jesus Christ.
You have received an anointing from the Holy One.
This anointing comes from God.
All of you know the truth.
passages.original: Καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου καὶ οἴδατε πάντες

passages.text: I have not written to you because you lack knowledge of the truth, but because you have it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
passages.sermon: I did not write to you because you do not know the truth.\r\nYou know the truth.\r\nNo lie comes from the truth.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἀλλ’ ὅτι οἴδατε αὐτήν καὶ ὅτι πᾶν ψεῦδος ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.
passages.sermon:
A liar is a person who denies that Jesus is the Christ.
This person is the antichrist.
The antichrist denies the Father.
The antichrist denies the Son.
passages.original: Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ψεύστης εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀρνούμενος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ὁ Χριστός οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἀντίχριστος ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν Πατέρα καὶ τὸν Υἱόν

passages.text: Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well.
passages.sermon:
John wrote to Christians who already know the truth.
He explained the relationship between the Son and the Father.
Anyone who denies the Son does not have the Father.
Anyone who confesses the Son has the Father also.
passages.original: πᾶς ὁ ἀρνούμενος τὸν Υἱὸν οὐδὲ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει ὁ ὁμολογῶν τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ τὸν Πατέρα ἔχει

passages.text: As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If it does, you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.
passages.sermon:
You are believers in Jesus Christ.
You have heard the truth about Jesus from the beginning.
Let this truth stay in your hearts.
If this truth remains in you, you will remain in the Son.
You will also remain in the Father.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς ὃ ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἐν ὑμῖν μενέτω ἐὰν ἐν ὑμῖν μείνῃ ὃ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἠκούσατε καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ μενεῖτε

passages.text: And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life.
passages.sermon: God made a promise to us.\r\nHe Himself gave this promise.\r\nThe promise is eternal life.
passages.original: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐπαγγελία ἣν αὐτὸς ἐπηγγείλατο ἡμῖν τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: I have written these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.
passages.sermon:
I am John, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
I wrote these things to you.
I wrote about people who try to deceive you.
These people want to lead you away from the truth.
passages.original: Ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν περὶ τῶν πλανώντων ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And as for you, the anointing you received from Him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But just as His true and genuine anointing teaches you about all things, so remain in Him as you have been taught.
passages.sermon:
You received an anointing from Him.
This anointing remains in you.
You do not need anyone to teach you.
His anointing teaches you about all things.
This anointing is true.
This anointing is not false.
Remain in Him, just as His anointing taught you.
passages.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρῖσμα ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μένει ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε ἵνα τις διδάσκῃ ὑμᾶς ἀλλ’ ὡς τὸ αὐτοῦ χρῖσμα διδάσκει ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων καὶ ἀληθές ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ψεῦδος καὶ καθὼς ἐδίδαξεν ὑμᾶς μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.
passages.sermon:
John writes to believers.  
He calls them little children.  
He tells them to remain in Christ.  
Christ is the Son of God.  
Christ will appear again.  
If you remain in Christ, you will be confident when He appears.  
If you remain in Christ, you will not be ashamed before Him at His coming.
passages.original: Καὶ νῦν τεκνία μένετε ἐν αὐτῷ ἵνα ἐὰν φανερωθῇ σχῶμεν παρρησίαν καὶ μὴ αἰσχυνθῶμεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.
passages.sermon: God is righteous.\r\nIf you know this, you also know something else.\r\nEveryone who practices righteousness has been born of God.
passages.original: Ἐὰν εἰδῆτε ὅτι δίκαιός ἐστιν γινώσκετε ὅτι καὶ πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὴν δικαιοσύνην ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγέννηται
